An inline intrusion prevention system drops packets that match a known exploit signature. Which control type and category does this represent?
Corrective, managerial
Preventive, technical
Preventive, physical
Detective, technical
An inline IPS stops the traffic before it reaches the target, so it is preventive, and it is implemented in technology. An IDS that only alerts would be detective.
A bank needs a tamper-resistant dedicated device to generate, store and use cryptographic keys for its payment applications. Which solution BEST meets this need?
Software-based key vault on a file server
Hardware security module
Trusted platform module on each laptop
Self-signed certificate on each application
An HSM is a dedicated, hardened appliance designed to generate and protect keys at scale. A TPM is bound to a single endpoint and is not meant for centralized application key services.
Which TWO actions should be part of a change management request for a production system upgrade?
Deleting the audit logs of the system beforehand
Documenting a backout plan
Skipping approval when the change is scheduled overnight
Applying the change directly on production without testing
Performing an impact analysis
Change management requires understanding impact and having a way to revert if the change fails. The other options bypass or undermine the control process.
In a Zero Trust model, which component sits in the data plane and actually allows or blocks the connection between a subject and a resource?
Policy administrator
Adaptive identity store
Policy enforcement point
Policy engine
The policy enforcement point is the gatekeeper in the data plane. The engine and administrator are part of the control plane and decide and instruct, rather than enforce.
A malicious insider hides confidential data inside the pixels of a company logo image and emails it out. Which technique is being used?
Salting
Steganography
Tokenization
Obfuscation of source code
Steganography conceals data inside another carrier file such as an image. Tokenization replaces sensitive values with surrogate tokens and is unrelated to hiding data in files.
A security architect wants the compromise of a web server's long-term private key to NOT allow an attacker to decrypt previously recorded TLS sessions. Which feature should be configured?
Certificate pinning
Session resumption tickets
Longer RSA key length
Perfect forward secrecy using ephemeral key exchange
Ephemeral Diffie-Hellman key exchange creates unique session keys that are not derived from the long-term key. A longer RSA key does not protect past sessions if the key is later stolen.
A company deploys a server cluster and redundant power supplies for its customer portal. Which part of the CIA triad does this primarily support?
Non-repudiation
Confidentiality
Integrity
Availability
Clustering and redundant power keep services running despite component failure, which is availability.
A system records which user deleted a file, and when it occurred. Which component of AAA provides this capability?
Authentication
Federation
Accounting
Authorization
Accounting tracks and logs user actions for auditing. Authentication proves identity and authorization determines permissions.
Why is a root certificate authority commonly kept offline in a PKI hierarchy?
Compromise of its private key would invalidate trust in every certificate beneath it
It allows the root to use symmetric encryption
Online root CAs cannot issue certificates
Offline CAs are required to publish CRLs
The root key is the trust anchor, so it is protected by being offline while intermediate CAs handle daily issuance. Root CAs can issue certificates whether online or not.
During a TLS session, which type of encryption is typically used to protect the bulk of the data after the handshake completes?
Digital signatures on each packet
Asymmetric encryption with the server's public key
Hashing with a salt
Symmetric encryption with a session key
Symmetric algorithms are much faster, so asymmetric cryptography is used only to exchange or agree on the session key. Hashing is not encryption.
A security team builds a set of decoy servers, switches and databases that mimics the production network to study attacker behavior. What is this called?
Honeypot
Honeynet
Honeytoken
Screened subnet
A honeynet is a network of multiple decoy systems. A single decoy host would be a honeypot, and a honeytoken is just a fake data item.
An attacker who has compromised one guest virtual machine manages to execute code on the underlying hypervisor and access other tenants' VMs. Which attack is this?
Container image poisoning
Cross-site request forgery
VM escape
VM sprawl
VM escape breaks the isolation boundary between guest and host. VM sprawl is an uncontrolled growth of VMs and is a management problem, not an attack technique.
Over several years, teams have created hundreds of virtual machines that nobody tracks, patches or decommissions. Which risk does this describe?
Resource reuse
VM escape
VM sprawl
Hypervisor rootkit
VM sprawl leaves unmanaged, unpatched systems that expand the attack surface. The remedy is lifecycle management, inventory and policy-based decommissioning.
A security researcher finds that a company's cloud object storage container holding customer invoices is readable by anyone on the internet. What is the MOST likely root cause?
A DDoS attack against the storage endpoint
A hypervisor flaw at the provider
A zero-day vulnerability in the storage service
Cloud misconfiguration of access permissions
Publicly exposed buckets are almost always the result of customer-side misconfiguration under the shared responsibility model. The provider's infrastructure is not at fault.
A developer pulls a container image from a public registry and deploys it to production. Later, the image is found to contain a cryptominer. Which control would have BEST prevented this?
Pulling only scanned and signed images from a trusted private registry
Running the container on a larger VM
Disabling logging in the container
Increasing CPU limits on the container
Image scanning and signing from a controlled registry verifies provenance and contents. Resource limits only constrain damage rather than prevent the malicious image being used.
A security analyst discovers a cloud access key committed in plaintext to a public source code repository. What should be done FIRST?
Revoke and rotate the exposed key
Enable versioning on the repository
Delete the commit from the repository history only
Notify all employees by email
Once exposed, the key must be assumed compromised, so it is revoked or rotated immediately. Deleting the commit does not help because copies may already exist.
Thousands of internet-connected cameras with unchanged factory passwords are hijacked and used to flood a website with traffic. Which weakness MOST directly enabled this?
Weak hashing of stored passwords
Lack of a web application firewall on the cameras
Default credentials on IoT devices
Unencrypted backup tapes
Default credentials let attackers log in at scale and enlist the devices in a botnet. Changing defaults during deployment would have prevented it.
An embedded controller in a medical device runs firmware that has a known vulnerability, but the vendor does not allow field updates. Which compensating approach is BEST?
Install antivirus software on the device
Move the device to the guest wireless network
Isolate the device on a restricted network segment
Enable automatic OS updates
When a device cannot be patched, segmentation limits exposure to it. Embedded devices usually cannot run antivirus agents, and updates are unavailable by the vendor's policy.
Attackers insert malicious code into a trusted software vendor's build pipeline, so customers receive a signed update that contains a backdoor. Which attack is this?
Brute force attack
Replay attack
Watering hole attack
Supply chain attack
The attacker compromises an upstream supplier to reach many downstream customers. A watering hole targets a website that victims visit rather than a vendor's software.
Which TWO of the following are common cloud misconfigurations that lead to data breaches?
Overly permissive IAM roles that grant wildcard access
Storage buckets set to public access
Enforcing multifactor authentication for administrators
Encrypting data at rest with customer-managed keys
Enabling audit logging for API calls
Excessive permissions and public storage are frequent root causes of cloud data exposure. The other options are good practices.
A container is started with the privileged flag and mounts the host's root file system. What is the MOST likely risk?
Expiration of the container's TLS certificate
Container breakout that gives control of the host
Duplicate IP addresses on the network
Slower application performance
A privileged container with host mounts removes isolation, so a compromise of the container can lead to full host compromise.

A web application running in a cloud VM fetches URLs supplied by users. An attacker supplies an internal address that returns the instance's temporary credentials. Which vulnerability is being exploited?
Directory traversal
Cross-site request forgery
Cross-site scripting
Server-side request forgery
SSRF tricks the server into making requests to internal resources, such as a cloud metadata service. XSS targets other users' browsers, not the server's outbound requests.

An accountant receives an email that appears to come from the CEO and asks for an urgent change to a vendor's bank account details. The email domain was legitimately registered and looks similar to the company's. Which attack is this?
Pharming
Business email compromise
Smishing
Credential stuffing
BEC uses impersonation of an executive or vendor to trick staff into financial actions. Smishing uses SMS rather than email.
An attacker with a stolen password database compares hashes against a very large table of precomputed hashes. Which control makes this attack impractical?
Adding a unique salt to each password before hashing
Adding a banner to the login page
Using longer usernames
Encrypting the database backups
Unique salts make precomputed rainbow tables useless because each password needs its own table. Backup encryption does not change how the hashes are stored.
A departing employee copies the customer database to a personal drive in the weeks before resigning. Which threat actor category BEST describes this person?
Nation-state
Insider threat
Unskilled attacker
Hacktivist
The individual abused legitimate access from inside the organization, which is the defining characteristic of an insider threat.
A newly discovered vulnerability is being exploited in the wild, and the vendor has not yet released a patch. What is this called?
Known false positive
Misconfiguration
Legacy vulnerability
Zero-day vulnerability
A zero-day has no available fix when exploitation begins. A false positive would be a scanner reporting a vulnerability that does not exist.
Users connect to a wireless network with the same SSID as the corporate network, but located in a nearby parking lot, and their traffic is intercepted. Which attack is this?
Bluejacking
Evil twin
War driving
Disassociation attack
An evil twin is a rogue access point that mimics a legitimate one to capture traffic. War driving only searches for wireless networks and does not intercept data.
An attacker captures a valid session token on the network and resubmits it later to gain access. Which mitigation BEST counters this attack?
Disabling ICMP
Using a larger hash output
Longer passwords
Short-lived tokens combined with nonces or timestamps
Replay attacks are defeated by making captured messages stale or single-use. Stronger passwords do not help because the attacker never needs the password.
While a user is logged in to an online bank, a malicious site causes the user's browser to silently submit a funds-transfer request to the bank. Which attack is this?
Buffer overflow
Cross-site request forgery
Cross-site scripting
SQL injection
CSRF abuses the authenticated session in the victim's browser to trigger actions the user did not intend. The attacker does not need to inject code into the bank's site.
A threat actor runs a malicious PowerShell script entirely in memory without writing any file to disk. Which malware type is this?
Logic bomb
Rootkit
Ransomware
Fileless malware
Fileless malware operates in memory using legitimate tools such as PowerShell, so it evades file-based scanning. The defining feature is the lack of a file on disk.
A user changes the account number in an API URL from /accounts/1001 to /accounts/1002 and receives another customer's data. Which weakness does this reveal?
Broken object-level authorization
Insufficient logging
Missing rate limiting
Weak TLS ciphers
The API does not verify that the requester is authorized to access the specific object. This is commonly called an insecure direct object reference.
An organization uses a SaaS email platform. Which item remains the customer's responsibility?
Updating the application code
Maintaining the physical data center
Patching the underlying operating system
Managing user accounts and data access settings
In SaaS the provider handles infrastructure and the application, but the customer is still responsible for its data, users and configuration.
A development team deploys code on a managed platform where the provider handles the operating system and runtime. Which responsibility stays with the customer in this PaaS model?
Replacing failed servers
Patching the runtime environment
Securing the application code and its data
Securing the hypervisor
In PaaS, the customer owns the application and data while the provider manages the platform underneath.
A team is moving event-driven code to a serverless function platform. Which practice BEST improves security?
Install host-based antivirus on the function runtime
Open inbound SSH for debugging
Give all functions the same administrator role
Assign each function a narrowly scoped, least-privilege role
Functions should have only the permissions they need to limit the blast radius. Customers have no access to the host runtime in serverless platforms, so host agents and SSH do not apply.

A microservices application's internal services communicate across a cluster. The architect wants each service to verify the identity of its peers and encrypt this east-west traffic. What should be implemented?
A single shared API key
Service mesh with mutual TLS
A perimeter firewall at the edge
Network address translation
A service mesh with mTLS authenticates and encrypts service-to-service traffic. A perimeter firewall does not inspect or protect traffic that stays inside the cluster.
Which statement correctly describes a difference between containers and virtual machines?
Containers cannot be isolated from one another
Containers share the host operating system kernel
Containers each include a full guest operating system
Containers require a hypervisor for each instance
Containers are lightweight because they share the host kernel, which also means a kernel flaw can affect all of them. VMs each carry their own guest OS.
A data center wants a hypervisor that runs directly on the server hardware, without a host operating system, to maximize performance and reduce attack surface. Which type should it choose?
Type 2 hypervisor
Type 1 hypervisor
Emulator running on a desktop OS
Container runtime
A Type 1 (bare-metal) hypervisor runs directly on hardware. A Type 2 runs on top of a host OS and is typical for desktops.
A company wants visibility into which SaaS applications employees use and wants to enforce data-protection policies between users and those cloud services. Which solution BEST fits?
Hardware security module
Web application firewall
Cloud access security broker
Network intrusion detection system
A CASB sits between users and cloud services to discover shadow IT and enforce policy such as DLP and access control. A WAF protects a specific web application, not user-to-cloud usage.
Which characteristic defines a software-defined network?
The control plane is separated from the data plane and managed by a central controller
All traffic must pass through a single physical firewall
It only works with wireless devices
Each switch independently makes routing decisions with no central logic
SDN decouples the decision-making control plane from the forwarding data plane, allowing centralized, programmable management.
A cloud-hosted application must remain available if an entire data center in a region fails. Which design BEST meets this goal?
Deploy several instances in the same rack
Deploy instances across multiple availability zones behind a load balancer
Take weekly snapshots of the VM
Use larger instances in a single zone
Spreading across independent availability zones removes the single data center as a point of failure. Snapshots help recovery but do not give continuous availability.
A factory robot controller must respond to sensor input within a guaranteed, fixed time. Which type of system is designed for this requirement?
Hypervisor-based virtual desktop
General-purpose desktop operating system
Real-time operating system
Network-attached storage appliance
An RTOS provides deterministic timing guarantees, which is critical in embedded and industrial control. General-purpose systems cannot guarantee response times.
An organization wants to protect programmable logic controllers in its plant from threats on the corporate network while still allowing necessary data exchange. Which design is BEST?
Allow remote desktop from the internet to the PLCs
Give the PLCs public IP addresses
Place the operational technology network in a separate segment behind a firewall
Place the PLCs on the same VLAN as user workstations
Segmentation with strict firewall rules limits what can reach ICS devices. Exposing or mixing them with IT systems greatly increases risk.
Which TWO are security constraints commonly associated with IoT and embedded devices?
Difficulty applying patches over a long device lifespan
Frequent vendor-driven automatic updates
Abundant memory for endpoint protection agents
Built-in support for enterprise single sign-on
Limited processing power for strong cryptography
Small, low-cost devices often cannot run heavy encryption or agents, and they remain deployed for years without patches. The other options describe the opposite of typical devices.
A security architect compares centralized and decentralized management of security policy. What is a key advantage of a centralized model?
Reduced need for documentation
Consistent policy enforcement and easier auditing
Faster local decisions without any coordination
Elimination of any single point of failure
Central management provides uniform policy and simpler oversight, though it introduces a single point of failure. That latter point is a strength of decentralized designs.
An operations team replaces cloud servers with freshly built images from a pipeline instead of patching running servers. What is this approach called?
Snapshot rollback
Immutable infrastructure
Shadow IT
Sandboxing
With immutable infrastructure, systems are never modified after deployment. Changes are made by redeploying a new, known-good image, which reduces configuration drift.
A web tier is configured so that all nodes handle requests at the same time, and if one fails the others absorb its load. Which configuration is this?
Active-passive
Warm site
Active-active
Cold standby
In active-active, all nodes serve traffic simultaneously. Active-passive keeps a standby that only takes over after a failure.
Virtual machines in the same data center subnet should not communicate unless explicitly allowed, to stop lateral movement after a breach. Which technique BEST accomplishes this?
Network address translation
Microsegmentation
Increasing the subnet size
Port mirroring
Microsegmentation applies granular policies between workloads, even within the same network segment, to restrict east-west traffic.
A cloud console log shows an administrator account signing in from two countries within ten minutes. The administrator confirms they did not do either one. What should be done FIRST?
Wait for more events to confirm
Delete the account's audit logs
Disable the account and revoke active sessions
Reset the password only after the next review
The pattern indicates compromised credentials, so the immediate step is containment by disabling the account and revoking sessions. Deleting logs would destroy evidence.
A network team wants to analyze which hosts communicate, how much, and over which ports, without capturing full packet contents. Which data source is BEST?
NetFlow records
Endpoint antivirus logs
Full packet captures
DNS zone files
NetFlow summarizes conversation metadata efficiently. Full captures provide payloads and require much more storage.
A vulnerability scan fails to report a flaw that is actually present on a server. How is this result classified?
True positive
False positive
True negative
False negative
A false negative means a real vulnerability was missed. A false positive would report a vulnerability that does not exist.
A company with many cloud accounts wants to continuously detect configuration drift, such as newly public storage, and compare settings to benchmarks. Which tool BEST fits?
Network access control
Endpoint detection and response
Cloud security posture management
Data loss prevention on email
CSPM monitors cloud configurations against policies and benchmarks and flags misconfigurations. EDR focuses on endpoint behavior.
An organization needs to scan files already stored in a SaaS application for sensitive data, without sitting inline in user traffic. Which CASB deployment mode is MOST appropriate?
Reverse proxy
API-based integration
Transparent bridge
Forward proxy
An API-based CASB connects out-of-band to the SaaS service and can inspect data at rest. Proxy modes work on traffic in transit.
A cloud virtual machine is suspected of being compromised. To preserve evidence for investigation, what is the BEST action before terminating the instance?
Delete the instance and restore from backup immediately
Reboot the instance to clear malware
Run a disk cleanup utility
Take a snapshot of the disk and, if possible, capture memory
Snapshots and memory captures preserve evidence. Rebooting or deleting the instance destroys volatile data and forensic artifacts.
A team has contained and removed malware from several servers. According to the standard incident response lifecycle, what should happen NEXT?
Preparation
Containment
Recovery
Detection
After eradication, systems are restored to normal operation during recovery. Lessons learned follows afterward.
What is the BEST approach for deploying a critical patch to production servers?
Test it in a staging environment, then roll out in phases with a rollback plan
Wait one year to see if others report problems
Apply it only to the test servers
Deploy to all servers at once to finish quickly
Testing and phased deployment catches problems early while limiting impact. Delaying critical patches leaves the organization exposed.
Which action BEST hardens a newly built Linux virtual machine in the cloud?
Keep the default administrator password until the first audit
Disable unused services and default accounts
Open every port in the security group
Enable all available network services for flexibility
Hardening removes unnecessary services and default accounts to reduce attack surface. The other options increase exposure.
Network engineers want to monitor and manage switches remotely with authentication and encryption of management traffic. Which protocol version should be used?
SNMPv1
SNMPv3
Telnet
SNMPv2c
SNMPv3 adds authentication and encryption, whereas versions 1 and 2c send community strings in cleartext.
A SOC wants to correlate detections across endpoints, network, email and cloud workloads in one platform for faster investigation. Which technology is MOST suitable?
Antivirus
Extended detection and response
Proxy server
Vulnerability scanner
XDR collects and correlates telemetry from several security layers. Antivirus is limited to endpoint file-based detection.
Which DNS-based email control lets a domain owner publish the mail servers authorized to send mail for the domain?
DNSSEC
SPF
DKIM
MX record
SPF lists the authorized sending hosts. DKIM signs messages, and an MX record only indicates where inbound mail is delivered.
A firewall contains a broad rule allowing all outbound traffic above a rule that denies traffic to a known malicious IP, and the malicious traffic is still passing. What is the MOST likely cause?
The firewall is stateless
The implicit deny rule is disabled
The rules are evaluated top-down and the allow rule matches first
The IP address is encrypted
Firewalls process rules in order and stop at the first match, so the specific deny should be placed before the broad allow.
Which authentication method is MOST resistant to phishing attacks?
FIDO2 hardware security key
Email-based one-time link
SMS one-time code
Security questions
FIDO2 keys bind authentication to the legitimate site's origin, so a fake site cannot capture a usable credential. SMS codes can be intercepted or relayed.
When an employee leaves, the company wants their access to all connected applications to be removed automatically. Which practice supports this?
Shared administrator credentials
Automated deprovisioning integrated with the identity system
Annual password resets
Manual email requests to each application owner
Automated deprovisioning removes access quickly and consistently. Manual processes tend to be delayed or missed.
A SOC analyst receives hundreds of low-severity alerts per day, causing real incidents to be overlooked. What is the BEST action?
Tune detection rules and thresholds to reduce noise
Stop reviewing low-severity alerts permanently
Disable all alerts
Add more analysts without changing rules
Alert tuning improves signal quality while keeping coverage. Disabling alerts removes visibility entirely.
Which standardized pair is used to share cyber threat intelligence in a machine-readable format between organizations?
SNMP and Syslog
SAML and OAuth
STIX and TAXII
TLS and IPSec
STIX defines the structure of threat intelligence data, and TAXII is the transport mechanism for exchanging it.
A company invites independent researchers to find and report vulnerabilities in its web applications in exchange for rewards. What is this program called?
Red team assessment
Vulnerability scanning
Bug bounty
Tabletop exercise
A bug bounty program pays outside researchers for responsibly disclosed findings.
A development team wants to find insecure coding patterns by analyzing source code without executing the application. Which technique should be used?
Fuzzing
Static application security testing
Penetration testing
Dynamic application security testing
SAST examines code at rest, while DAST tests the running application.
Which backup strategy BEST protects against ransomware that tries to encrypt or delete backups?
Maintain immutable or offline copies of backups
Use only incremental backups
Back up to the same server
Store backups on a mapped network drive that is always writable
Immutable or offline copies cannot be altered by malware that compromises the production network. Always-writable drives are exposed to the same attack.
A company leaves a cloud provider and must ensure its data cannot be recovered from the provider's shared storage. Physical destruction of drives is not possible. Which method is BEST?
Cryptographic erase by destroying the encryption keys
Deleting the files from the console
Formatting the virtual disk
Emptying the recycle bin
If data was encrypted, destroying all copies of the key renders it unreadable. Simple deletion leaves data recoverable.
Which control can prevent users from resolving domain names associated with known malware command-and-control servers?
MAC filtering
Port security
DNS filtering
Disk encryption
DNS filtering blocks or sinkholes resolution of known malicious domains before a connection is made.
Which TWO log sources would be MOST useful for investigating a suspected compromised cloud account?
Print server job logs
Conference-room booking logs
Cloud audit trail of API activity
Building HVAC controller logs
Identity provider sign-in logs
API audit logs show what actions were performed, and sign-in logs show how and from where the account authenticated. The other sources are unrelated to account activity.
During an investigation, an analyst cannot correlate events from several servers because the timestamps differ by several minutes. What should be implemented?
Additional firewalls
Log compression
Larger log storage
Time synchronization using NTP
Consistent time sources are essential to build accurate timelines. Storage and compression do not fix timestamp drift.
A security team gathers stakeholders to walk through a ransomware scenario around a table to test the plan without touching production systems. What is this exercise?
Vulnerability assessment
Tabletop exercise
Penetration test
Full failover test
A tabletop is a discussion-based exercise used to test decisions and communications with no operational impact.
A single loss event is expected to cost $50,000 and is expected to occur once every five years. What is the annualized loss expectancy?
The cost of mitigating a low-impact risk is greater than its expected loss, and senior management formally signs off on leaving it as is. Which risk response is this?
Acceptance
Avoidance
Transference
Mitigation
Knowingly tolerating the risk with documented approval is acceptance. No controls are added or contracts transferred.
A customer wants proof that a vendor's controls operated effectively over a six-month period. Which report is MOST appropriate?
SOC 2 Type I
Vulnerability scan results
Vendor marketing brochure
SOC 2 Type II
A Type II report tests control operation over time, whereas Type I describes controls at one point in time only.
Before sharing detailed network diagrams with a prospective vendor, which document should an organization require?
Service-level agreement
Statement of work
Memorandum of agreement
Non-disclosure agreement
An NDA legally protects confidential information during discussions. An SLA defines service performance and would come later.
Which activity BEST reduces risk before onboarding a new cloud service provider that will process regulated data?
Selecting the cheapest provider
Relying solely on the provider's website
Performing vendor due diligence and security assessment
Signing the contract and assessing later
Due diligence evaluates the vendor's controls before data is shared. Assessing after signing leaves the organization exposed.
Within a data governance program, which role holds accountability for setting a dataset's sensitivity label and approving who may access it?
Data custodian
System administrator
Data processor
Data owner
The data owner is accountable for classification and access decisions. The custodian carries out technical handling under the owner's direction.
The legal department notifies IT of pending litigation. What should happen to relevant data that would normally be deleted according to the retention schedule?
It is anonymized immediately
It is preserved under a legal hold
It is deleted on schedule
It is moved to a public share
Legal hold suspends normal deletion so potentially relevant evidence is preserved.
Under the GDPR, a data controller must generally notify the supervisory authority of a personal data breach within how long of becoming aware of it?
30 days
24 hours
7 days
72 hours
The GDPR sets a 72-hour deadline for notifying the authority where feasible and required.
Which of the following is a possible consequence of failing to comply with applicable regulations?
Lower cyber insurance premiums
Reduced audit frequency
Fines and sanctions
Automatic certification renewal
Non-compliance can lead to fines, sanctions, loss of licenses and reputational damage. The other options would be benefits, not consequences.
A regulator wants independent assurance that a company's controls meet a required standard. Which type of audit provides this?
Self-assessment
Internal audit
External audit
Peer code review
External auditors are independent of the organization and can provide credible attestation to third parties.
A system administrator is terminated for cause. What should HR and IT do FIRST?
Wait until the exit interview ends next week
Ask the employee to delete their files
Disable the user's accounts and revoke access
Delete the user's mailbox
Immediate revocation protects against retaliation or data theft. Deleting data could destroy evidence.
A company wants to test its disaster recovery capability by restoring systems at the alternate site while production keeps running normally. Which test is this?
Walk-through
Tabletop exercise
Full interruption test
Parallel processing test
In a parallel test, recovery systems are brought up and verified alongside production without any interruption of it.
Which metric describes the average time a system operates before it experiences a failure?
MTBF
RTO
MTTR
RPO
Mean time between failures measures reliability. MTTR measures how long repair takes.
Which business continuity metric defines the maximum acceptable time a system can be down after a disruption?
Recovery point objective
Mean time between failures
Annualized rate of occurrence
Recovery time objective
RTO is the target time for restoring service, while RPO measures acceptable data loss.
A security manager tracks the number of unpatched critical vulnerabilities each month as an early signal of rising risk. What is this measure called?
Key risk indicator
Risk register
Service-level agreement
Recovery time objective
A KRI is a metric that signals changes in risk exposure before an incident occurs.
An organization has a policy requiring encryption of sensitive data. Which document would specify the exact steps administrators follow to enable it on a given system?
Standard
Charter
Guideline
Procedure
Procedures give step-by-step instructions to carry out policy. Standards define mandatory specifications rather than the steps.
A retailer stores and processes payment card data. Which compliance framework applies specifically to it?
HIPAA
SOX
PCI DSS
FERPA
PCI DSS governs organizations that handle cardholder data. HIPAA covers health information and SOX covers financial reporting.
Which TWO items are typical outputs of a business impact analysis?
Identification of critical business functions
A penetration test report
Vulnerability scan results for all hosts
A list of firewall rule changes
Recovery time and recovery point targets
A BIA identifies which functions are critical and sets recovery objectives for them. The other items belong to technical security testing and configuration activities.
